title: Storage layers in Postgres
caption: Heap code asks the buffer manager for pages, and only on a cache miss does smgr and md.c read the table file from disk.

title: Life of an INSERT
caption: Follow numbers 1 to 8 to see a big row get shrunk, placed in a pinned buffer page, and cleaned up later.

badges.meaning: heap_insert starts and prepares the tuple
Big values are compressed or moved to a TOAST table
hio.c finds a page with room using the free space map
ReadBuffer pins the page in shared buffers
On a cache miss, the clock sweep picks a victim buffer
md.c reads the 8kB block from the data file
PageAddItemExtended adds the tuple, then the buffer is dirtied and WAL written
Pruning and VACUUM clean up dead tuples later

title: Anatomy of an 8kB page
caption: A page has a header and line pointers at the top, tuples growing up from the bottom, and each tuple starts with its own header.

badges.meaning: PageHeaderData, 24 bytes at the start of the page
Line pointer array, one 4 byte entry per tuple
Free space between pd_lower and pd_upper
Tuples stored from the end of the page backwards
